title: Edge model variant selection and compression lab journal
body:
Context:
We ran a short, focused lab to determine practical model+quantization choices for a retail-edge POC. Customer constraints: deployable on their on-prem inference appliance (NVIDIA T4 equivalent, 16GB GPU memory), strict 95th-percentile latency target <= 200 ms for single-turn product-query completions, and an operational cost objective roughly equivalent to <= 0.6x their current microservice cost per inference. Data is privacy-sensitive (no external hosting), so Private deployment + KMS is required.

Objective:
- Produce a ranked set of candidate model variants that meet latency and memory constraints while preserving retrieval-quality >= baseline (their current rules-based answers).
- Create reproducible quantization settings and prompt-pipeline changes to hit the SLA.
- Capture practical fallbacks and rollout suggestions for Redwood Private.

Experiment notes (high-level):
We tested 4 base model families with the customer’s sample workload (3k real queries + synthetic tail):
- Mistral-7B-instruct (baseline: FP16)
- Llama2-13B-chat (baseline: FP16)
- Falcon-7B-instruct (baseline: FP16)
- Smaller distilled candidate: Redstone-3B-like mimic (internal distillation artifact)

Quantization/compression approaches tried per model:
- FP16 (no compression) — reference for quality/latency
- INT8 (PTQ, per-channel) — NVidia-supported kernel, reduced mem footprint
- NF4 + GPTQ (8-bit-ish WF optim) — AWQ/GPTQ style; more aggressive but riskier on hallucination
- KV cache eviction trimming (truncate past-kv to 512 tokens for long queries)

Selected metrics and measurement method:
- p95 latency measured with steady-state 1 qps, collectors at 10k requests each config (cold start excluded), measured on T4 emulator machine with same config as customer node.
- Tokens/sec and peak GPU memory from nvidia-smi logs.
- Quality proxy: correctness@top1 (binary match vs gold where available) + answer-length and hallucination-flag (manual spot checks, 300 samples).

Raw results (abridged):
- Mistral-7B - FP16: p95=180ms, peak GPU mem=11.2GB, correctness=87%
- Mistral-7B - INT8: p95=140ms, peak mem=7.0GB, correctness=85% (small regressions on rare entity disambiguation)
- Mistral-7B - NF4+GPTQ: p95=125ms, peak mem=6.6GB, correctness=82% (noticeable style shifts, some noun-drop hallucinations)

- Llama2-13B - FP16: p95=340ms, peak mem=18.1GB (exceeds device), correctness=91%
- Llama2-13B - INT8: p95=260ms, peak mem=12.0GB (still >16? note: spills to host), correctness=88%
- Llama2-13B - NF4+GPTQ: p95=220ms, peak mem=11.6GB, correctness=86% (borderline for SLA, memory still tight)

- Falcon-7B - FP16: p95=210ms, peak mem=12.6GB, correctness=86%
- Falcon-7B - INT8: p95=165ms, peak mem=8.2GB, correctness=84%

- Redstone-3B-like - FP16: p95=95ms, peak mem=4.8GB, correctness=78%
- Redstone-3B-like - INT8: p95=80ms, peak mem=3.2GB, correctness=76%

Interpretation and quick wins:
- Best single-run fit for customer SLA+memory is Mistral-7B INT8 or NF4-GPTQ. Both fit inside 16GB with p95 <= 150ms for INT8, 125ms for GPTQ. The Mistral family retained higher correctness relative to compressed Llama2 variants under our dataset.
- Llama2-13B is a quality leader but not a practical fit at this hardware point unless the customer accepts a multi-GPU node or offloading.
- The 3B distilled artifact is the fastest/cheapest but falls short on correctness; could be a reranker candidate (see pipeline notes).

Prompt and pipeline tuning applied:
1) System message simplification: removed verbose safety boilerplate; shortened context to keep model decoding steps minimal. Net p95 drop ~6–8% across variants.
2) Few-shot examples: moved to prompt pre-caching (cache tokenized prefix across similar queries). Saved ~12% token-generation overhead for repeated patterns.
3) Truncation strategy: implement smart prefix-preserve (keep last 256 tokens + heuristic summary of earlier text) — reduced average input length by 30% for long queries without quality loss in 92% of manual checks.
4) Two-stage pipeline: short-circuit answer generation with Redstone-3B for 70% of trivial queries (detected via a classifier), fallback to Mistral-7B INT8 for others. End-to-end p95 reduced; cost down ~0.5x.
5) Reranker: use 3B as fast scorer to re-rank the top-3 outputs from compressed 7B model when uncertainty-high flag is set. This tradeoff adds ~25ms but reduces unsafe/hallucinated answers by ~40% on sampled set.

Operational notes for Redwood Private deployment:
- Recommend shipping Mistral-7B INT8 as v1 on the appliance image with NV inference kernels. Provide an alternate NF4-GPTQ image for customers wanting extra latency headroom (but call out slight quality regressions).
- Default rollout: canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% with auto-fallback: if p95 breach >10% for 3 consecutive 5m windows, route to lightweight hosted fallback if customer allows; else fallback to CPU-based slower path and notify.
- Memory tuning: enable per-process memory limits and GPU memory reservation to avoid host-page spills observed for Llama2-13B INT8.

Risk register / unresolved items:
- Dataset bias: our 3k sample skewed toward product-description queries; entity-heavy customer support dialogs are underrepresented. Need additional 1k examples from customer.
- GPTQ reproducibility: some runs of NF4+GPTQ produced unstable tokenization marginally affecting numeric answers. Need deterministic seed and post-quant validation harness.
- Licensing check for distilled internal Redstone artifact (legal to ship in Private images?). Ping legal.

Next steps / action items (owner tags):
- Collect additional entity-rich examples from customer (Diego) — due 2025-01-25.
- Add deterministic seed + validation harness for GPTQ builds (Lina) — due 2025-01-12.
- Prepare Private appliance image with Mistral-7B INT8, integrate KMS hooks, and smoke tests (Priyanka) — due 2025-02-02.
- Workshop runbook: create a step-by-step 'edge-deploy-checklist' for customer ops (Aisha) — due 2025-01-22.

Quick checklist for handoff to solutions sales / customer success:
- Summary slide: Mistral-7B INT8 recommended, Llama2-13B requires heavier infra (multi-GPU).
- Demo script: show two-stage pipeline with quick fallback to 3B for trivial queries.
- Risk slide: quantization hallucination risks + need for more entity data.
- Pricing note: estimate 0.45x cost using two-stage pipeline vs current microservice baseline (approx).

Lab log appendix (short traces):
- Example failure case (Mistral NF4): numeric price dropped by 30% on answers involving SKU IDs when logits truncated at beam edge; workaround: add SKU-in-context few-shot examples and increase temperature clamp.
- Example success case: Redstone-3B correctly classed 72% of 'availability-check' queries as trivial and served immediate canned response; hybrid flow saved ~120 ms on average.

Free-form notes to self (informal):
- Customer excited about single-node Private solution — selling point is consistent latency and no data egress. Keep messaging on Mistral+INT8 stability.
- Consider automated eval “quality delta” that combines BLEU-ish with entity-accuracy for next workshop.

Attachments and artifacts: see linked_artifacts above and the attached raw bench logs in GitHub PR.

End of journal entry.
